DIRECTORS’ REPORT
Financial Performance
In its second year of operation, the Company focused on building a strong foundation while
navigating a challenging external environment marked by economic uncertainty and high
inflation. The Company laid the groundwork for future growth and sustainability. The focus
remained on strengthening operational frameworks and positioning the Company for long-term
success.

Economy
In FY24, Pakistan's economy demonstrated signs of recovery after a contraction in FY23 (GDP: 0.2%), achieving a GDP growth rate of 2.4%. Key positive indicators include growth in the
agricultural sector, easing inflationary pressures, an improved current account balance, and a
stabilization of the PKR/USD exchange rate due to increased foreign exchange reserves. However,
challenges remain, particularly in manufacturing activity and the high cost of debt servicing,
which consumes 56% of total revenues. While authorities have managed to stabilize the economy,
the outlook continues to face significant downside risks from both external and internal factors.
Amid this transitional phase, the Real Estate sector has emerged as a critical driver of economic
growth and prosperity. By leveraging its potential and seizing emerging opportunities, the sector
can play a vital role in shaping a more prosperous future for Pakistan and its citizens.

Real Estate / REIT Sector
Pakistan’s Real Estate sector has historically been a vital pillar of the economy, delivering
attractive returns for investors and addressing the housing needs of its expanding population.
However, recent political instability and economic challenges have posed difficulties for the
sector. As FY24 concluded, there is renewed optimism for economic reforms and stability. While
the sector grew by 9.1% in FY23, growth slowed to approximately 6.4% in FY24. Real Estate
Investment Trusts (REITs) are emerging as a significant force in Pakistan’s real estate market,
offering investors a streamlined path to passive income and portfolio diversification. Their ability to
attract both institutional and retail investors positions them as a key element of the investment
landscape. Supportive regulatory reforms by the SECP have lowered entry barriers and spurred
unprecedented investment in the REIT sector. As of the end of FY24, 28 REIT Management
Companies (RMCs) are registered with the SECP, with 15 REIT schemes approved, boasting a
cumulative fund size of Rs. 161.21 billion. Among these, 3 REIT schemes are listed on the Pakistan
Stock Exchange, with a combined market capitalization exceeding Rs. 66.43 billion.
The future of REITs in Pakistan looks bright, driven by increasing investor interest, regulatory backing,
and evolving market dynamics. Continued innovation, investor education, and regulatory
improvements are expected to further accelerate the growth of REITs, contributing significantly to
the development of Pakistan’s property market.

Governance
The Company adopts a forward-thinking approach to corporate governance, ensuring full
adherence to the Listed Companies (Corporate Governance) Regulations, 2019 (CCG). Our
compliance statement, which has been reviewed and approved by external auditors, is featured
in this annual report, reflecting our dedication to maintaining the highest levels of governance
and transparency.

Board of Directors
The Company prides itself on having a strong and diverse Board of Directors, consisting of
individuals with a wide array of skills, expertise, and experience. This diversity ensures a wealth of
perspectives and knowledge, enabling the Board to effectively steer the Company’s strategic
direction. The Board currently includes seven (7) members, with four (4) Non-Executive Directors
(NEDs) representing shareholders and two (2) Independent Directors (IDs). Current composition of
the Board is as under:

Male Non-Executive Directors (NED):

2. Mr. Tanzain Shafqat

Independent Directors
5. Mr. Kamran Nasir
6. Mr. Sadiq Ali

Chief Executive Officer – Executive Director
7. Mr. Adil Ahmed Kamal
Mr. Zeeshan Ali Khan is the Chairman of the Board.

Annual Evaluation of the performance of the Board, Board’s Committees and
Individual Directors
In line with the Listed Companies (Code of Corporate Governance) Regulations 2019, the
Company has implemented a structured and rigorous process for the regular evaluation of the
Board, its members, and its Committees. This assessment framework covers a broad spectrum of
criteria, such as Board composition and diversity, the effectiveness of Board and Committee
operations, governance structures, and overall dynamics and contributions. This comprehensive
approach ensures a detailed and well-rounded evaluation of performance.

Compensation for Directors
Independent Directors are paid a fixed fee for attending Board meetings, as approved by the
Board. The CEO, who is the only executive director on the Board, along with non-independent
directors, the Company Secretary, and the CFO, are employees of the Zameen Group. As such,
they do not receive any remuneration from the Company. Additionally, the CEO is not paid any
extra fees for attending Board meetings.

Directors’ Compliance Statement
The Board affirms the following:
- Proper books of accounts have been maintained.
- The financial statements prepared by management accurately and fairly reflect the Company’s
financial position, operational results, cash flows, and changes in equity.
- There is no significant uncertainty regarding the Company’s ability to continue as a going concern.
- Appropriate accounting policies, consistent with International Financial Reporting Standards (as
applicable in Pakistan), have been applied in the preparation of the financial statements. Accounting
estimates, where necessary, are based on reasonable and prudent judgment.
- The internal control system is well-designed, effectively implemented, and consistently monitored.
- There have been no material deviations from the best practices of corporate governance.

Audit and Risk Oversight Committee
In compliance with the Code of Corporate Governance, the Audit and Risk Oversight Committee has
continued to operate in accordance with its Terms of Reference, which have been formally approved
by the Board.

Internal Audit
The Internal Audit function of the Company operates efficiently within the framework outlined in the
Listed Companies (Code of Corporate Governance) Regulations, 2019, as well as the charter
approved by the Audit and Risk Oversight Committee. The Board highly values the insights and
recommendations provided by the Audit and Risk Oversight Committee regarding the adequacy and
effectiveness of the Company’s internal controls and ensures timely and appropriate actions are taken.
Currently, internal audit function is established in-house.

Ethics & Compliance
In compliance with the Listed Companies (Code of Corporate Governance) Regulations, 2019, the
'Code of Conduct' has been shared with all Directors of the Company.

Appointment of Auditors
KPMG Taseer, Hadi & Co. Chartered Accountants, the auditors of the Company for FY 2023-24, are
retiring and, being eligible, have offered themselves for reappointment for the term 2024-2025. The
Audit Committee and the Board recommend their reappointment as statutory auditors for the year
2024-2025, subject to the approval of their remuneration by the general body at the Annual General
Meeting. This remuneration will also cover the charges for the Compliance Statement under Corporate
Governance practices as per the Listed Companies (Code of Corporate Governance) Regulations,
2019.
The external auditors have received a satisfactory rating under the Quality Control Review Program of
the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Pakistan (ICAP). They have confirmed compliance with the
Listed Companies (Corporate Governance) Regulations 2019 and the International Federation of
Accountants (IFAC) guidelines on the Code of Ethics, as adopted by ICAP.
Additionally, the external auditors have not been engaged to provide any other services that could
impair their independence, and they have confirmed adherence to IFAC guidelines in this regard.

Related Party Transactions
In adherence to the REIT Regulations and the Code of Corporate Governance, the Company
submitted all related party transactions to the Audit and Risk Oversight Committee and the Board of
the Company for review and approval. These transactions were subsequently approved by both the
Audit and Risk Oversight Committee and the Board of Directors during their respective meetings. Further
details of these related party transactions are outlined in Note 14 of the accompanying audited
financial statements.

Acknowledgement
The Board of Directors extends its heartfelt gratitude to the Securities and Exchange Commission of
Pakistan (SECP) and other relevant government agencies for their invaluable guidance and
cooperation. The Board also expresses its sincere thanks to the shareholders for their continued trust
and support, as well as to the Board Committees for their significant contributions and assistance. Their
collaboration has greatly strengthened the Board’s ability to fulfill its responsibilities effectively.
Additionally, the Board recognizes and deeply appreciates the unwavering dedication and hard work
of the Management and employees, whose efforts have been pivotal to the Company’s success.
For and on behalf of the Board,

Mr. Adil Ahmed Kamal
Chief Executive
